questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Leave more space between your car and the car in front of you.
Do not drive if you feel tired.
Check that your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: It is harder to see at night. Take steps to make night driving safer for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. If you feel tired while driving, stop driving right away.

questions.question: What affects how far your car travels before it stops?

options.text: How fast your car is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance is affected by your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other drugs makes both stronger and more dangerous. For example, one drink plus a cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you do?

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are near.
Signal only if other cars are near.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are near.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not skip signaling. Make it a habit to always signal.

questions.question: Before you start the car, what should you check?

options.text: That backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
That adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
That child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
That everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: That everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Make it a routine before driving. Buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs as well.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means it is not safe to enter the road or driveway from your direction. If you see this sign, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Who should wear a seat belt?

options.text: All occupants every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt every time. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object and can hurt others.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with red lights on?

options.text: You cannot pass the bus. It is illegal.
You do not need to stop.
You only need to stop if you see children.
You do not need to stop if you are in a school yard.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass the bus. It is illegal.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass a stopped school bus with red lights on, even in a school yard. Exception: You may pass on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and move out of their way. Trying to get revenge risks making the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal traffic rules as if there were no construction.

questions.explanation: You must slow down and follow directions from signs, flaggers, or police in construction zones. Not following these directions is illegal and dangerous for workers.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you only drink a few drinks.
Dangerous only to the person who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs. It puts you and everyone on the road at risk.

questions.question: Which statement about bicyclists is true?

options.text: They have the legal right to ride on most roads.
They have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers.
They must use hand signals before turning.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists can legally ride on most roads except interstates. They follow the same traffic rules as cars. They must signal turns with hand signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is entering from the right.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, when a stop sign is present, or when red lights flash and gates are down.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see railroad crossing signs, slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop. If red lights flash or gates are down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.
